headline: High: shared browser/MCP-style tooling and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and action-cascade risks; compliance risk is lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a ingests browser and runtime-injected MCP/hook outputs, while agent_b is an orchestrator that can consume workflow inputs. No shared channel is explicitly documented, so the pathway is inferred rather than proven; uncertainty pushes this above low. The pair could be bridged through files or messages if configured.
conditions: IF agent_a is configured to pass browser or MCP output into agent_b inputs, injection becomes reachable.
IF a shared workspace or message queue is added between the agents, attacker-controlled content can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Disable automatic parsing of browser/MCP text as instructions.
Add a manual review step before agent_b consumes agent_a output.
Restrict shared channels to typed, schema-validated fields.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches session history, project code, and provider auth data, and has broad network egress; agent_b also has broad egress. Even without a documented shared filesystem, any shared workspace or copied output could leak sensitive context from agent_a through agent_b. The evidence is indirect, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a workspace or copied artifacts, sensitive files can flow between them.
IF agent_b is given agent_a session history or auth prompts, those data classes can be exfiltrated over network egress.
mitigations: Keep separate directories and credentials for each agent.
Redact auth prompts before any handoff.
Block network egress for agent_b on sensitive runs.
Review and delete shared temp files after each task.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can spawn subprocesses and uses task-scoped isolation; agent_b is a data-engineering orchestrator with only a GitHub API surface documented. There is no evidence of overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so direct conflict is not established. If a shared repo or filesystem is introduced, conflict risk rises.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same repository or directory, concurrent edits can conflict.
IF agent_b is extended with filesystem write tools, overlap with agent_a becomes material.
mitigations: Assign one writer per directory or repo.
Serialize edits through a single queue.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Check in small changes frequently.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can produce browser-derived content and project edits, while agent_b is an automation/orchestration system that may act on upstream workflow metadata. The profiles do not prove blind trust, but the pairwise pathway exists if agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative. Because the downstream blast radius can include automated actions, medium is warranted.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without verification, errors can cascade into downstream workflow actions.
IF agent_a's browser-derived facts are used as inputs to automation, incorrect facts can propagate.
mitigations: Require a verification step before agent_b acts on agent_a output.
Limit agent_a output to citations and raw evidence only.
Have agent_b cross-check critical facts against source systems.
Log and review automated actions for a trial period.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles provider authentication data and session history, while agent_b only touches workflow metadata. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so a compliance breach is not established. The risk is limited to potential policy mismatch if sensitive agent_a data is routed into agent_b's broader automation context.
conditions: IF provider auth data from agent_a is routed into agent_b logs or workflows, retention policy mismatch may occur.
IF the deployment places EU or regulated data into agent_b without matching controls, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of workflow metadata.
Set short log retention for agent_a outputs.
Review data-class mappings before enabling handoff.
Restrict access to auth prompts.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls per agent.
